video_title: Why Event Sourcing Exists: History Is The Product
thumbnail_text: State is a view, log is truth
core_insight: Event sourcing keeps an append-only log of domain facts so current state is a derived fold of history, enabling audit, temporal queries and fan-out, at the cost of complexity.

scenes.voice: You need to answer what happened, not just what is. CRUD gives you balance = 1024. It erases how you got there.
scenes.visual: Split screen: left shows a database row being overwritten balance 1000 → 1024, right shows a question mark over a timeline with missing steps.

scenes.voice: Audit, debugging, multiple views, business rules on past state. Overwriting rows also creates write contention and hard merges.
scenes.visual: Four icons appear: audit seal, bug with timeline, multiple views, lock on row. Quick highlight of contention.

scenes.voice: The obvious fix is CRUD plus an audit table. Simpler, but audit is secondary, schema changes hurt, and replay is manual.
scenes.visual: Simple CRUD box with an audit table attached by a thin line. Red X over replay arrow.

scenes.voice: Event sourcing flips the model. You never update a balance, you append MoneyDeposited and MoneyWithdrawn. State is a left-fold of the log.
scenes.visual: Ledger style list growing downwards: AccountOpened, DepositRecorded, MoneyWithdrawn. A derived balance counter updates on right.

scenes.voice: Commands are validated against the aggregate rebuilt from events. Valid commands emit new events. Projectors build read models from the log.
scenes.visual: Flow diagram animates step by step.
scenes.on_screen_text: Command → Aggregate → Event Store → Projector → Read Model
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Client -- Command --> Service
  Service -- Load events --> Aggregate
  Aggregate -- New events --> EventStore[(Event Log, append-only)]
  EventStore -- Stream --> Projector
  Projector -- Upserts --> ReadModel[(Read DB / Views)]
  ReadModel -- Queries --> Client

scenes.voice: This helps when auditability is first class, you need temporal queries, or one fact must fan out to many views at different speeds.
scenes.visual: Trading account example: events stream to three boxes: AccountBalance view, RiskExposure view, AuditTrail.

scenes.voice: The trade-off is complexity. Events are immutable, so schema evolution needs upcasting. Reads are eventually consistent. Replay cost needs snapshots and idempotent projectors.
scenes.visual: Scale balancing complexity on left vs audit/temporal/fan-out on right. Small callouts: versioning, eventual consistency, snapshots.

scenes.voice: Mental model: think ledger not snapshot. The event log is the source of truth, the aggregate is the interpreter, state is a derived view.
scenes.visual: Ledger book morphs into a database snapshot with an arrow labeled derived.
scenes.on_screen_text: Log is truth, state is derived

mental_model: Treat the domain as a ledger of immutable facts. Current state is a left-fold of the append-only event log; the aggregate interprets the log, projectors derive views. Choose event sourcing when history is the product, not when you only need current state.
final_takeaway: Event sourcing preserves why state changed. State is a view, the log is the truth.
